description: Japanese glossary of the game's own text (docs/modding/translation-handbook.md). terms: English term of glossary_en.json -> the Japanese form used in every file. keep_latin: Latin words the validator accepts in the Japanese text. style: the rules of voice and form.

style.voices: Harry: first person 私, plain male speech (だ/か/だろう), calls Cybil and Lisa 君, Kaufmann and Dahlia あんた. Cybil: 私, brisk, light feminine endings (わ/のよ/ね), calls Harry あなた. Lisa: 私, informal and soft (の/わ/よね), calls Harry あなた; polite です/ます only on the video tape, where she speaks to the doctor. Kaufmann: 私, curt and superior (だ/かね/のだ), calls Harry 君. Dahlia to Harry and Kaufmann: 私/我ら, prophetic literary speech (ぬ/であろう/がいい/のだ), calls Harry お前; Dahlia to Alessa: ママ about herself, sweet and commanding (のよ/なさい/わね), calls her お前. Alessa and Cheryl: child speech; Mommy/Mama is ママ, Daddy is パパ.
style.narration: Harry's observations of objects are plain だ/である sentences; prompts to the player are polite questions (取りますか？ 押しますか？). Notes and newspapers are terse, noun-ended; Lisa's diary is short plain sentences.
style.quotes: 「 」 for the [ ] of the English; a dash or a run of noise is ― (U+2015); the ellipsis is one … (U+2026).
style.width: digits, PTV and the initial K are half-width ASCII; punctuation (？！、。) is full-width; no spaces between words, an intended blank is U+3000.
style.line_breaks: at phrase (bunsetsu) boundaries; no line starts with a closing mark, a small kana or ー (kinsoku); at most 25 full-width characters per message line, 16 per item name, 22 per description line.
style.item_in_sentence: an item name inside a sentence is the inventory name unchanged: '<name>がある。取りますか？', '<name>を使った。', '<name>を手に入れた。'
